description: A feature flag read inside the ad service's `GetAds` handler activated a singleton `CPULoad` that spawned 4 daemon threads each running a tight `Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis())` loop; the threads pinned CPU cores and saturated container CPU and `jvm_cpu_recent_utilization_ratio` on the `ad` service.
mechanism: The flag is read in [`AdService.java#L172`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/AdService.java#L172): on every `getAds` gRPC call, `CPULoad.getInstance().execute()` is invoked with the boolean value of the `adHighCpu` flag. When the flag is `true`, [`CPULoad.java#L46-L52`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L46) calls `spawnLoadWorkers(4)`, which launches 4 daemon threads ([`CPULoad.java#L64-L74`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L64)). Each thread runs a tight `while(shouldRun) { Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis()); }` loop ([`CPULoad.java#L101-L103`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L101)), saturating CPU cores with continuous logarithm calculations. The threads persist until the flag is toggled off, at which point `stopWorkers()` sets `shouldRun=false` on each thread. Because the workers are spawned only once (guarded by the `running` flag at line 49), repeated `getAds` calls while the flag is on do not create additional threads.

variants.description: CPU utilization ratio of the ad container. The adHighCpu flag spawned 4 tight-loop Logarithmizer threads, causing the ad container's CPU utilization to spike from ~0.19 to ~389 (a ~2000x increase).
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is ~0.14-0.19 (with occasional spikes to ~0.26-0.34). At 23:35 UTC, one minute after the incident time, the value jumps from ~0.17 to ~405.3 — a ~2400x increase — and remains sustained around 385-395. This is the clear onset of the CPU spike.

variants.description: Count of runnable daemon threads in the ad service JVM jumped from 13 to 17, exactly matching the 4 Logarithmizer daemon threads spawned by CPULoad.spawnLoadWorkers(4).
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is a steady 13. At 23:36:00, one minute after the incident marker, the value jumps to 17 (a ~31% spike) and remains elevated at 17-18 for the rest of the series. This is the first timestamp showing the clear departure from baseline.

variants.description: JVM CPU utilization ratio for the ad service jumped from ~0.02% to ~50%, directly caused by the 4 Logarithmizer daemon threads running tight Math.log() loops that saturate CPU cores.
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is ~0.0002 (0.02% CPU). At 23:36 the value jumps to 0.174, a ~870x increase, clearly the first timestamp where the spike begins. The prior point at 23:35 (0.000237) is still within normal baseline range.

variants.description: Average HTTP server latency for frontend GET requests (served via frontend-proxy) spiked from ~10ms to ~190ms as a cascading effect of the slow ad service, since frontend pages fetch ads on each render.
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is roughly 10-11ms. At 23:35 (one minute after incident time), the value jumps to 12.21, beginning a clear upward trend that accelerates through 17, 18, then dramatically to 47, 123, and beyond. This is the first timestamp showing a departure above the stable ~10-11ms baseline.

variants.description: Feature flag impression counter for adHighCpu with variant 'on' appeared (went from non-existent to 1) when the flag was toggled on, directly confirming the adHighCpu flag activation by flagd.
variants.onset_reasoning: This is a 'created' metric — the time series did not exist before the incident. The first data point appears at 23:35:00 UTC, which is the earliest timestamp in the series and occurs right after the incident time (23:34:36 UTC). This marks the moment the feature flag began being evaluated with the 'on' variant.

logs.name: ad: High CPU-Load problempattern enabled (INFO)
logs.description: At 23:34:49.787 UTC, the ad service emitted 26 INFO logs announcing that the High CPU-Load problem pattern had been enabled.
logs.cause: Smoking-gun direct evidence of the adHighCpu flag. On every getAds invocation, AdService.java:172 calls ffClient.getBooleanValue("adHighCpu", false, ctx) and passes the result to CPULoad.execute(enabled). When enabled=true, CPULoad.java:48 logs "High CPU-Load problempattern enabled" at INFO and, if not already running, spawns 4 daemon Logarithmizer threads (CPULoad.java:50, 64-73) that tight-loop Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis()) to saturate CPU. Note the log is not an error — the ad service continues serving requests successfully, just under CPU pressure.
logs.source: ad service (Java, oteldemo.problempattern.CPULoad logger via OpenTelemetry Java agent)
